quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face and eyes in a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it invites the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
Does not affect safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it invites the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may cause the passing driver to return to your lane too early.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake and rear brake at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front brake and rear brake at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply controlled pressure to both brakes at the same time. Avoid locking the brakes.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is usually most easily seen by other drivers when riding in which lane position?
questions.explanation: The center lane position is best for visibility. It places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if needed.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and metal plates or utility covers.

questions.question: __________ can cause motorcycle collisions.

options.text: Honking the horn at the wrong time

questions.explanation: Following too closely behind another vehicle is a major cause of motorcycle collisions. Keep a safe distance when riding behind other vehicles.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before moving. Never try to cross before a train.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean do not pass. Dashed white lines mean you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: As you consume more alcohol, your ability to safely ride:
questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink more alcohol. Do not ride your motorcycle if you have consumed any alcohol.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Watch the road far ahead of you while riding. This helps you spot dangers early and react to them before they become a problem.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, you should:
questions.explanation: Wearing bright clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you at any time of day.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you be seen, avoid hazards, and escape danger. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane, not invite them.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent and use them to steer. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you stay balanced when turning.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT strongly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol you drink

questions.explanation: Your BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not play a major role.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should:

options.text: Ride near the front of the group.
Ride at the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, behind the leader. This lets experienced riders lead and watch the less experienced riders at the same time.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard for drivers to see your turn signals, you should:

options.text: Keep using your mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to warn other drivers of turns.

questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is important to clearly communicate with other drivers.

questions.question: Before riding, check your throttle. When released, it should:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check that your throttle snaps back quickly when you release it. Your clutch should also feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Encourage others to use your lane.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you be seen, avoid hazards, and gives you an escape route if danger appears. It should keep other drivers out of your lane.

questions.question: It is illegal to ride a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: In California, anyone 21 or older cannot ride with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. People under 21 cannot ride with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Even lower BAC levels can make riding unsafe.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake may prevent you from developing the skill to use the front brake properly when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: When entering a turn, what is best?

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may proceed through the intersection with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must come to a complete stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in the direction you want.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride at the same speed as you would during the day.
Ride more slowly than you would during the day.
Ride faster than you would during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride more slowly at night, especially on unfamiliar roads. Slower riding gives you more time to spot and avoid hazards when it is dark.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Do not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is acceptable to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between rows of stopped or slow-moving vehicles is dangerous. Other vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to operate safely.
